newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares fall in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares fall in listless trade.

text.p: Norwegian shares slipped in thin trade on Monday in a market lacking impulses, brokers said.
The Total index closed 0.68 percent lower at 1,175.79 points in trade worth just 624 million crowns.
"Things are quiet today. The oil prices are down, the crown is weaker. It is generally a poor market without any impulses," one broker said. "If the U.S. market falls we will continue to fall here."
Industrial group Norsk Hydro was the most traded share at 126 million crowns, but it fell 1.3 percent to 381 crowns to help burden the Total index.
Stavanger-based Smedvig was the second most traded share at 41 million crowns and one of the few bright spots on a gloomy day. Smedvig's A share climbed 2.50 percent to 185 crowns.
"There was some demand for Smedvig after it lost ground earlier," a broker said.
But forestry groups Norske Skog and Moelven both ended sharply lower after announcing that they had dropped talks on merging their units for saw mills and board production.
